title: User Manager backend: users, roles, groups, permissions, effective access, Supabase Auth Admin provisioning
objective: Port the full User Manager API surface: user CRUD/deactivate with Supabase Auth identity provisioning/linking/disable, role CRUD with usage visibility, group CRUD with member/role/permission subresources, permission catalog listing, and the effective-access view — per-tenant scoping throughout, all changes audited (P-03, section 12 User Manager).
scope: Users: list/create/get/update, deactivate (not delete), tenant assignments (>=1 tenant unless Internal), direct role and permission assignment per tenant, group membership management, effective-access view endpoint
Roles: list/create/get/update, disable/delete with usage visibility endpoint (which users/groups reference the role)
Groups: list/create/get/update, disable/delete; subresources for members, roles, direct permissions

Supabase Auth integration: creation provisions an auth user via the Admin API (email; password flow per reference behavior — invite/temporary password consistent with the .NET+Keycloak behavior adapted to GoTrue), links auth_user_id; deactivation disables the auth user (ban) so sign-in fails
implementation_details: Mirror the reference endpoint paths and DTOs from the .NET Users/Roles/Groups endpoint files exactly (A-3); user creation collects first name, last name, email (required).

Provisioning flow: create app users row + auth user atomically-as-practical — auth-side failure must roll back the app row (or compensate + surface error); duplicate-email handling per reference semantics.
Deactivate: is_active=false + Auth Admin ban/disable; reactivation path mirrors reference behavior; deactivated users rejected at T-011 middleware.
Role disable requires usage check surface (roles-in-use warning/blocking per reference behavior — verify implemented behavior and port it).
Per-tenant scoping: role/permission/group assignments carry tenant context; a user may differ per tenant (P-03).
Effective-access endpoint reuses computeEffectivePermissions (T-012) — no duplicate logic.

unit: None new (effective-permission logic already unit-tested in T-012)
integration: User create provisions a local Supabase Auth user, links auth_user_id, and the new user can sign in; deactivate blocks sign-in and API access
Role/group CRUD + assignment matrix persists and feeds effective-access correctly (fixture-based expectations)
Normal user requires >=1 tenant; Internal user may have zero; per-tenant assignment isolation (role in tenant A grants nothing in tenant B)
Permission matrix per endpoint (403 without user-management permissions); all changes produce audit rows
e2e: User Manager spec + RBAC visibility spec adapted in T-043

history.message: Task generated by Planner from approved spec.md. Maps to P-03, A-4 Admin API, section 12 User Manager, P-13 audit.

T-017 implemented: users/roles/groups/permissions/effective-access routes, Supabase Auth Admin provisioning with compensation, per-tenant assignment model, self-lockout and grant-no-higher-than-self guards, audit on every mutation. 44 tests added (938 total). All gates green. 9 mutants applied and killed.

Evaluator verdict: PASS. Suites re-run alone: users.test.ts + roles-groups.test.ts + auth-wiring.test.ts = 58/58 EXIT=0; full-suite baseline green (938/938). Routes confirmed tenant-scoped (/users,/roles,/groups,/permissions absent from GLOBAL_ROUTE_PREFIXES) with requirePermission on every route and isReadAccessible/isWriteAccessible or requireVisibleUser on every by-id path; denial renders the uniform 404 (no cross-tenant existence oracle). FOUR of the implementor's 9 mutants re-run first-hand, each proven applied by grep before running: MUTANT-1 (requireVisibleUser confinement removed) KILLED by exactly 'confines list and by-id access to members of the ambient tenant (F-027)'; MUTANT-2 (callerHoldsInAllScopes=true) KILLED by exactly the 3 claimed tests across both suites; MUTANT-3 (grantApplies drops tenant scope) KILLED by exactly 'resolves per-tenant assignments independently: tenant A grants nothing in tenant B' — per-tenant scoping is real, not assumed; MUTANT-4 (requireWritableGroup drops isWriteAccessible) KILLED by 'confines every by-id group route to the ambient tenant'. TWO evaluator-original mutants also KILLED: E1 (user.updated audit write suppressed) killed by the PUT test — audit coverage is asserted beyond create; E2 (activate gate weakened users.deactivate->users.view) killed by the 403-matrix test, which pins the exact required permission string per route using a users.view-only caller. All mutants reverted; residue grep clean; suites re-green 58/58. FIVE FLAGGED DECISIONS RULED, all ACCEPTED: (1) GET /permissions from the seeded table gated on roles.view — the seeded table is what the FKs accept, and V-040 demands the seeded catalog exactly; (2) activate gated on users.deactivate — the catalog is fixed (P-03), users.activate does not exist, and adding a code would ripple through seed.sql/SPA mirror/drift guards; read as the user-lifecycle permission this is correct; (3) provisioning failure as 422 USER_AUTH_PROVISIONING_FAILED — verified problem.ts sanitizes every status >=500 (constant detail, code dropped), so a 5xx would violate AC-031's typed-error requirement; 422 for an upstream dependency is semantically imperfect but the right call inside this contract; (4) compensating deletion of the orphaned auth identity — a deliberate improvement over the reference's accepted orphan, required in spirit by AC-031 ('no half-created app user') since an orphan makes the address permanently un-creatable; covered by the compensation test; (5) one userManager buildApp slot — cohesion decision, wiring pinned for both composition roots by auth-wiring tests. Security: auth-admin.ts is the sole service-role touchpoint, key read only via config module; initial password random, never returned/logged; create-path auth error message deliberately not propagated (email echo); built SPA bundle scanned first-hand — zero occurrences of any server-only literal or the service-role JWT payload. Residual obligation: V-039 e2e user-manager spec belongs to T-043.

Schema conformance (CLAUDE.md: all generated JSON must conform to .claude/schemas/). These blocks were written by the implementor/evaluator as TOP-LEVEL keys the task schema does not allow. They are substantive audit records, so they are PRESERVED VERBATIM here rather than deleted. Moved: implementation_notes, test_results.

routes_ported: GET/POST /api/v1/users, GET/PUT /users/{id}, POST /users/{id}/deactivate, GET /users/{id}/effective-access (UserEndpoints.cs:30-35, permission for permission)

GET/POST /api/v1/groups, GET/PUT /groups/{id}, POST /groups/{id}/disable, POST /groups/{id}/members, POST /groups/{id}/members/{userId}/remove, POST /groups/{id}/roles, POST /groups/{id}/permissions (GroupEndpoints.cs:31-39)
GET /api/v1/permissions (NEW: no .NET reference route; spec s375 + AC-030)
POST /api/v1/users/{id}/activate (NEW: no .NET reference route; AC-029 + V-038 require reactivation)
measured_semantics: already inactive -> 409 (UserEndpoints.cs:111) while its 422 siblings are unprocessable
roles/groups mappers attach a `code` extension and render detail as 'CODE: message'; the tenants mapper does not. Both preserved as-is.
decisions_without_reference: GET /permissions gated on roles.view; reads the SEEDED permissions table rather than the TS catalog constant so offered codes are exactly the codes the FKs accept.
POST /users/{id}/activate gated on users.deactivate: the permission catalog is FIXED (P-03) and has no users.activate code; adding one would change seed.sql, the SPA mirror and the drift guards.

Auth provisioning failure maps to 422 USER_AUTH_PROVISIONING_FAILED, not 5xx: lib/errors/problem.ts sanitizes every status >= 500 (detail replaced, code dropped), which would violate AC-031's 'typed error'.
Provisioning COMPENSATES on app-side failure (deletes the auth identity), improving on the reference's accepted-orphan behaviour, because an orphan makes the address permanently un-creatable.
Initial password is server-generated, random, never returned or logged; the user reaches the account via the best-effort recovery link (emailSent), mirroring the Keycloak reset-password email.
One buildApp slot (`userManager`) registers all four routers rather than four slots: they are one feature.
unmapped_dotnet_behavior: IKeycloakAdminService.SendResetPasswordEmailAsync has no exact GoTrue analogue; ported as auth.admin.generateLink({type:'recovery'}) with the same best-effort/emailSent semantics.
Keycloak 'enabled' flag has no GoTrue equivalent; disable is implemented as an indefinite ban (ban_duration), which refuses sign-in as AC-029 requires.
